units.note: Opening Greek clause (καὶ Ποπλίῳ τῷ πατρὶ περιπέσῃ συμφοραῖς) and closing περὶ ταύτην run across the chapter seams; the English handles both without loss of sense.
Numbers (25,000 foot, 2,500 horse, seventh day) check. Philip = Philip V; the English is unambiguous in context.

findings.quote: Opposite it on the west is another hill in a corresponding position
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna: τούτῳ δ᾽ ὁ * ἀπὸ τῆς δύσεως ἀντίκειται. A word (probably the hill's name or a qualifier) has dropped out after ὁ; the English supplies 'another hill' and reads on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: Opposite it on the west is the [...] hill, in a corresponding position

units.note: Lacuna is short (likely one word). The 20/10/2 stades figures and compass points all check.
2,000 men, third hour, 1,000 halved, two stades all check. Gaius = Gaius Laelius, consistent with ch. 9.
